name: Integrations
usage: Use only the parts that apply; delete the others with their tests. Webhooks (src/webhook.mjs): read the raw body with readRawBody(req) (1 MB cap), then verifyWebhook({ secrets, body, signature, timestamp, replay }) with the provider's signature and timestamp headers, the shared secret from config (WEBHOOK_SECRET, never in the repo; list two while rotating) and one memoryReplayStore() per process, or a shared store with the same claim(key, expiresAtMs) contract (a unique-key insert) when the app runs more than one instance. It checks an HMAC-SHA256 over '<timestamp>.<raw body>' in constant time, a 5-minute window and replays; answer 400 on any IntegrationError and parse JSON only after it passes. A provider with its own signing scheme (Stripe, Razorpay) uses its official verifier instead, still with the window and the replay store. Payment events (src/events.mjs): createEventLedger({ rank }) and apply({ id, objectId, type, version }, handler): version is the provider's event time or sequence per object, rank orders event types that share a version (later states higher); duplicates and events older than the object's last applied one are not applied, and a failing handler records nothing so the provider's retry is applied. Keep the store in the database (applied event ids with a unique key, last order per object, in one transaction with the handler's write) when the app runs more than one instance. Cache (src/cache.mjs): createCache({ ttlMs }) — every entry expires; read with get(key, loader) and change data only through write(keys, writer), which drops the keys before and after the write so no read returns the old value afterwards. Third-party tokens (src/token-vault.mjs): createTokenVault({ keys: loadTokenKeys(TOKEN_KEYS), scopes }) with TOKEN_KEYS='<id>:<32-byte base64 key>' from the server's secret store (openssl rand -base64 32; put the new key first to rotate, then rewrap stored records) and scopes = the least scopes the app needs per provider; ask the provider for scopesFor(provider, need) only, seal() what it returns (a broader grant is refused), store the record, and open(record, { provider, owner, need }) only for the signed-in owner. Never log a token, a key or a signature.
